newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha weaker, backwardation remains steep.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha weaker, backwardation remains steep.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices eased in afternoon trade on Thursday in sympathy with bearish overnight crude oil markets, traders said.
The backwardation in naphtha"s inter-month spreads remained steep, however, reflecting tightness in prompt supplies.
The one-month spread from first-half April was quoted at plus $9.00/10.00, little changed from Wednesday"s levels.
Bids for second-half March/second-half April were heard at $10.00, although no offers emerged.
Traders said at least four buyers were seeking second-half March cargoes amid scarce availability.

Second-half April open-spec naphtha was bid at $232.00 a tonne, against offers at $233.50. It was traded at $235.00 on Wednesday. Also on Wednesday, first-half May was sold to a Japanese trading house at $230.00.
First-half April was quoted at $237.00/239.50 on Thursday, down from late Wednesday"s $241.00/243.00.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders were said to be looking for an additional allocation from Indonesia for February lifting, with most of the initial allotment already placed.
